eli5.text: If you have the Max plan, your coding assistant now switches to a stronger model for deep thinking and for reviewing your code changes, and it does so more quietly, since the review step only runs on meaningful edits rather than every little keystroke. Behind the scenes, the assistant merges its two thinking modes into one, stops asking for your permission to think hard, and removes old debug logging so the process feels smoother. Your work history and file retention settings also got cleaner, and the assistant now keeps track of a few more details when summarizing long conversations.

ai.title: codesearch maxResults per-file limit and global cap
ai.summary: code_search now enforces a per-file maxResults limit (default 15) and a global cap of 250 results. Backend tool definitions and common params updated to reflect this behavior. CLI tool-handlers implement grouping and truncation logic. Truncation notices indicate skipped files or excess matches.

eli5.text: When you search for something in your project's files, the assistant now shows you a limited number of matches: up to 15 results per individual file, and no more than 250 results total across all files. If a file has more matches than the limit, only the first 15 are shown, and if the overall search hits the 250-result cap, the rest are skipped; the response will tell you when either of these limits was reached. This change went live on 2025-10-08 and applies to everyone using code search, preventing overwhelming or slow responses from very broad or repetitive searches.

eli5.text: The assistant can now find and inspect files in a project by name pattern, like asking to see every config or test file at once. A new file-finder lets it search using patterns such as "*.json" or "src/**/*.ts" and a directory-listing tool shows what files sit in a given folder. Both tools are live today, and the finder returns results sorted by most recently modified, capped at 15 matches per search with a hard limit of 250 across all searches.

Callers must pass logger to prevent undefined reference errors during credit operations.

eli5.text: When the system handles organization billing actions like checking usage or spending credits, it now requires a "logger" (a tool that records what happens) to be passed along with every call. Previously, some calls were missing this logger, which could cause errors when performing credit operations, like running out of credits mid-action with no record of why. This is a behind-the-scenes stability fix affecting how the backend tracks organization billing; it is already live and does not change any visible billing behavior, just makes the billing functions more reliable.

ai.title: Inject logger into org-monitoring functions
ai.summary: Refactors `packages/billing/src/org-monitoring.ts` to accept a `logger` instance via parameters instead of importing a global singleton. Updates `sendOrganizationAlert`, `monitorOrganizationCredits`, `trackOrganizationUsageMetrics`, and `validateOrganizationBillingHealth` to use the passed-in logger. Replaces direct error logging with `getErrorObject` for consistent serialization in catch blocks.

eli5.text: The system now lets each part of the organization-monitoring code receive its own logging tool as a parameter, instead of all of them sharing one single global logger that is imported from a central location. As a result, each function records alerts and errors through a logger that is handed to it, and unexpected problems are serialized consistently using a shared helper. If you watched the monitoring functions run, you would not see different behavior, but the internal code is tidier and easier to maintain.
